title: hibiscus brackenridgei subsp. molokaianus
intro: Hibiscus brackenridgei subsp. molokaianus, commonly known as the Molokai hibiscus, is a rare and endemic subspecies of the hibiscus plant native to the island of Molokai in Hawaii. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including the treatment of fever, digestive issues, and inflammation. The therapeutic actions of the Molokai hibiscus are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as flavonoids, saponins, and phenolic acids, which exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. Additionally, the plant is rich in vitamins and minerals, including vitamin C, calcium, and iron, making it a nutritious and potentially therapeutic addition to a healthy diet.
